text: A website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru: patients book visits, emergency info, plus doctor profiles, a health blog, and Kannada/Hindi versions

@CEO Charter needs three calls the brief leaves open. Budget is 60. Minimum full scope (emergency section 10, booking form 15, doctor profiles 10, one blog post 10, Kannada and Hindi 24, styling 5) costs 74, so something must give.
1. Q1 Scope vs budget (60 units). A: English only with all features (emergency 10, booking 15, profiles 10, one blog post 10, styling 5 = 50), Kannada/Hindi deferred, 10 left for fixes. B: Both languages but no blog post and no styling (emergency 10, booking 15, profiles 10, languages 24 = 59), no room for fixes. C: English plus one language is 62, over budget, so not available. Trade-off: A delays the language requirement from the brief, B ships it but plain-looking, with no blog and no buffer. Identity recommends A, since a bilingual site with zero fix budget risks failing Audit. Choose A or B.
2. Q2 Booking behaviour. The site is one static file with no backend, so it cannot store or send bookings itself. A: form validates input and shows a confirmation plus the hospital's phone number, with the request sent by mailto or a third-party form service to a hospital address the Requester supplies. B: form is a clearly labelled demo that stores nothing, with phone booking shown as the real route. Which do we commit to? A is an external commitment and needs a receiving address from the Requester.
3. Q3 Facts and risk authority for emergency info. A: use only Requester-verified numbers, addresses and doctor details, and pause the run to ask @Requester before build. B: use national numbers (108 ambulance, 112 emergency) plus clearly marked placeholders for hospital-specific details and sample doctors, to be replaced before launch. Wrong emergency data is a patient-safety risk. Identity recommends A for emergency info, with B allowed for doctor profiles and blog text. Choose A, B, or the split.

@Identity Decisions: Q1 A, Q2 A with a placeholder address, Q3 B with emergency placeholders marked and no pause.
1. Q1: A. English only with emergency, booking, profiles, one blog post and styling (50 units), leaving 10 for fixes. Kannada and Hindi are deferred and logged as an open item. I chose A because B ships no blog and no buffer, so it drops a brief item anyway and risks failing Audit. Trade-off accepted: the language requirement is delayed.
2. Q2: A. The form validates input, shows a confirmation and the hospital phone number, and sends the request by mailto. The brief is silent on the receiving address, so I chose the simplest option: a clearly marked placeholder address, tracked as an open input for @Requester to replace. The form must say plainly that the request is sent by email and is not a confirmed appointment until the hospital replies.
3. Q3: B, applied strictly to emergency info. Show the national numbers 108 (ambulance) and 112 (emergency). Hospital-specific details (address, phone, directions, emergency desk) appear as visibly marked placeholders such as 'To be confirmed by CityCare'. Doctor profiles and blog text are sample content, also labelled. Do not pause the run for the Requester, since Requester-only facts are tracked as open inputs and never block done. Never present a placeholder as a real hospital number. I did not use Identity's A because it would hold the run on a Requester answer.

@Adaptation Charter recorded from the CEO's Q1 A, Q2 A and Q3 B. Scope is English only, 50 of 60 units, 10 held for fixes. Propose workflows within that scope; Kannada and Hindi stay deferred as an open input.

@Priority I propose five single-part workflows that build the one file in order, totalling 50 of 60 units and leaving 10 for fixes. Each one has a completion check that can be read directly from the file.

proposal.name: Create file with emergency section
proposal.goal_gap: No site file exists and there is no emergency information.
proposal.expected_outcome: A single HTML file with page skeleton, header, and an emergency section showing 108 and 112 plus marked placeholders.
proposal.completion_check: File is one HTML document with no build step. Emergency section shows 108 labelled ambulance and 112 labelled emergency. Hospital address, phone, directions and emergency desk each show a visibly marked placeholder such as 'To be confirmed by CityCare', and none looks like a real number or address.

proposal.name: Add booking form with validation and mailto
proposal.goal_gap: Patients have no way to request a visit.
proposal.expected_outcome: A booking form that validates required fields, builds a mailto to a marked placeholder address, and shows a confirmation.
outputs: booking form section and inline JavaScript in citycare.html
proposal.completion_check: Empty or malformed required fields (name, phone, email, date) are rejected before sending. Valid submit builds a mailto link to a marked placeholder address and shows a confirmation with a hospital phone marked as a placeholder. The form or confirmation says the request is sent by email and is not a confirmed appointment until the hospital replies.

proposal.name: Add sample doctor profiles
proposal.expected_outcome: A doctor profiles section with sample profiles clearly labelled as sample.
proposal.completion_check: Section contains at least two profiles, and each profile and the section heading carry a visible 'Sample content' label.

proposal.name: Add one sample health blog post
proposal.expected_outcome: One short health blog post labelled as sample content.
proposal.completion_check: File contains exactly one blog post with a title and body text, and a visible 'Sample content' label.

proposal.name: Add responsive styling
proposal.goal_gap: The sections are unstyled and may not be readable on mobile.
proposal.expected_outcome: Inline CSS giving a consistent, readable layout that adapts to narrow screens.
proposal.completion_check: File has inline or CDN CSS covering all sections with consistent fonts, spacing and colours, plus a media query or flexible layout that keeps content readable at 360px width without horizontal scrolling.

text: @Adaptation GRANT for all five workflows: 50 of 60 units by rate card, 10 stay unspent as the fix reserve. Each envelope caps money at the rate-card cost with one retry. A failed completion check after the retry stops the workflow, and any fix that needs the reserve must come back as a new proposal.

@Coordination Registered W-1 Create file with emergency section, W-2 Add booking form with validation and mailto, W-3 Add sample doctor profiles, W-4 Add one sample health blog post, W-5 Add responsive styling. Budget: 50/60 used.

@Builder run W-1 first: it has no dependencies and creates citycare.html, which W-2, W-3 and W-4 all need. All five workflows write to the same file, so only one runs at a time. W-5 runs last because it needs the booking form, profiles and blog to exist. Rule: Dependency order first; among workflows that are ready, lowest registration number first; one workflow per turn because citycare.html allows a single writer..

@Identity All 9 done-when items pass on a direct read of site v5. One warning on item 4: the name check uses /^\p{L}[\p{L} .'\-]{1,79}$/u, which excludes combining marks (\p{M}), so a name in Devanagari or Kannada script (for example "मीरा") should be rejected. I read the regex and did not run it. A fix would cost 8 units from the 10 reserve, and whether to spend it is your decision. I did not render the page at 360px, so item 9 rests on the CSS rules alone.

Done. Audit passed all 9 done-when items on site v5, each read directly from the file. The one warning (item 4) does not fail the item: the name check rejects empty and malformed names, which is what the item requires. I am not spending 8 of the 10 reserve units on it. The site is English only, and Latin-script names work. Two caveats are unverified: the regex was read, not run, and the 360px layout was read from CSS, not rendered. Follow-ups for the Requester, none blocking: replace the placeholder email, hospital details, sample doctors and sample blog; decide on funding Kannada and Hindi (about 24 units). Add the name regex fix (allow combining marks, \p{M}) to that list, since it will matter once Kannada or Hindi is funded.

Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence. Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): Receiving email address for booking requests (placeholder in use).; Hospital address, phone number, directions and emergency desk details (placeholders in use).; Real doctor names, specialties and details to replace the sample profiles.; Real or approved blog content to replace the sample post.; Kannada and Hindi versions: deferred for budget; needs a decision on funding (about 24 units for both) and translated or reviewed text.; No Kannada or Hindi content is required in the file, and no text in the file should claim a placeholder is a verified hospital detail (tracked here, not a done-when item).. Site v5 is in the preview. Requester: tell us if you want changes.
